brief: North Macedonia's payments infrastructure layer is small, concentrated and almost entirely non-listed: the settlement layer is NBRM's MIPS (RTGS, live since 2001), the retail clearing layer is Клириншка куќа КИБС АД, and the card switching/processing layer is Интернационален Картичен Систем АД (CaSys), with Diners Club MAK as a minor non-scheme issuer and NBRM as the designator and overseer of all three. The richest recurring disclosures are KIBS' own statistics page and NBRM's payment statistics and oversight pages; operator press releases (kibs.mk news, casys.com.mk MEDIA) carry launch-level detail but are JS-rendered and need a headless fetcher, and nbrm.mk answers plain fetches with 403, so bot-tolerant collection is a prerequisite rather than an optimisation. Because none of these operators publish investor-relations material, financial depth for the cell must come from Central Registry filings surfaced via aggregators, supplemented by trade press (bankarstvo.mk, ecommerce.mk, faktor.mk) that republishes processor announcements and reports ownership deals. The dominant forward story to monitor is the TIPS-clone instant-payment initiative connecting MK with Albania and Kosovo, which currently has no consumer brand and must be tracked on programme terminology ('иницијатива за инстант плаќања').
